source: segmentation (Blender simulation render, background replaced by plain white)

camera.motion: static (no background texture to check directly; both animals keep constant image y of feet/top and constant apparent size, consistent with a fixed camera)
camera.perspective: no ground plane, horizon or vanishing point visible (white background). Both animals walk left->right along image x with constant bbox height and constant foot line y~799-800 px: motion is essentially parallel to the image plane at a constant depth. Feet of both animals at the same image row (~800 px), so both are likely on the same ground line; the rabbit is just ahead of (and possibly slightly in front of) the creature.

objects.name: creature
objects.description: large fantasy quadruped (antelope/goat-like beast, orange-brown body, long striped curved horns sweeping backwards, white/grey muzzle, long tufted tail)
objects.distinguish: the big animal; only large object
objects.motion: walks steadily to the right (+x image), no vertical drift; leg/tail swing cycle ~40 frames (bbox width oscillates 542..617 px)

bbox_w_px.note: tail tip to muzzle tip incl. swinging tail and backward horns; varies with gait

objects.reference_point_note: true origin (root) not visible; ref_x/ref_y = bbox centre, centroid_x/y = mask centroid (more stable horizontally: step sd 0.77 px vs 1.68 px for bbox centre)

objects.name: rabbit
objects.distinguish: small animal at the creature's front feet, bottom-right of the creature
objects.motion: hops to the right alongside/just ahead of the creature; hop period ~13 frames, feet lift only ~8 px

bbox_w_px.note: nose/ear to tail, varies with hop pose

bbox_h_px.note: ear tip to feet; drops to ~58 when crouched/stretched mid-hop

objects.reference_point_note: ref = bbox centre; centroid also given (nearly identical)

image_motion.note: per-frame step pulses with each hop (fast ~10-11 px in frames after take-off, slow ~5 px near landing)

static_objects: none (plain white background, no ground features or props)

relations.note: the two move together at nearly the same image speed (~7.7-7.9 px/frame); the rabbit's bbox overlaps the creature's bbox in x (under the muzzle) but masks never touch

events.what: both animals already moving at frame 0 and still moving at frame 74 (no start/stop in clip)
rabbit take-off (feet bottom rises from ~801 to ~793 px)
creature lowest hoof lifted (bbox bottom 790-795 instead of 799): gait phase
